1 | # Waypoint — Adaptive Codebase Onboarding
     2 | 
     3 | Waypoint turns Python, JavaScript, TypeScript/TSX, Java, HTML, and CSS repositories into an
     4 | evidence-aware code graph and a role-specific onboarding workspace. It uses
     5 | static analysis only: analyzed repository code is never imported or executed.
     6 | 
     7 | ## Architecture
     8 | 
     9 | ```mermaid
    10 | flowchart TD
    11 |     UI[React + TypeScript UI] -->|HTTP /api/v1| API[FastAPI application]
    12 |     API --> IMPORT[Local path or secured GitHub clone]
    13 |     IMPORT --> ANALYZER[Python AST + Tree-sitter analyzers]
    14 |     ANALYZER --> GRAPH[Typed code graph]
    15 |     ANALYZER --> INDEX[Revision-aware SQLite index]
    16 |     INDEX --> SEARCH[FTS5/BM25 + local vectors]
    17 |     GRAPH --> SEARCH
    18 |     API --> MEMORY[SQLite conversations and sessions]
    19 |     API --> AGENT[Repository agent runner]
    20 |     AGENT --> INVESTIGATE[Investigation model]
    21 |     INVESTIGATE --> TOOLS[Bounded repository tools]
    22 |     TOOLS --> SEARCH
    23 |     TOOLS --> GRAPH
    24 |     AGENT --> SYNTHESIZE[Synthesis model]
    25 |     SYNTHESIZE --> VALIDATE[Pydantic tool + answer + citation validation]
    26 |     VALIDATE --> UI
    27 |     UI --> COMPARE[Independent two-agent comparison]
    28 |     COMPARE --> TOOLS
    29 |     MCP[MCP server: 30 tools] --> GRAPH
    30 |     MCP --> SEARCH
    31 |     HOOKS[Pre / post / error hooks and JSONL traces] -.observe.-> API
    32 |     HOOKS -.observe.-> AGENT
    33 |     HOOKS -.observe.-> TOOLS
    34 | ```
    35 | 
    36 | FastAPI and Pydantic provide typed HTTP boundaries and generated OpenAPI; React,
    37 | TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, React Flow, and Monaco provide the interactive evidence
    38 | workspace. SQLite keeps the project locally deployable while persisting graph sessions,
    39 | chunks, lexical/vector indexes, issues, and conversation memory. The model layer supports
    40 | OpenRouter, the Anthropic API, and the Claude Agent SDK. In dual mode a low-cost model can
    41 | investigate through tools while a stronger model synthesizes a validated answer.
    42 | 
    43 | The detailed verification package, including coverage, Flask HTTP E2E, live multi-step
    44 | agent evidence, and same-question two-model comparison, is in
    45 | [`verification/README.md`](verification/README.md). Significant AI-assisted engineering
    46 | interactions are recorded in [`prompts.md`](prompts.md).
    47 | 
    48 | ## What is included
    49 | 
    50 | - Python AST extraction for modules, classes, functions, methods, imports, and calls
    51 | - Tree-sitter extraction for JavaScript/JSX, TypeScript/TSX, Java, HTML, and CSS
    52 | - ES module imports/re-exports, CommonJS `require`, Java packages/imports, lexical
    53 |   containment, and conservatively inferred calls
    54 | - Explicit class-instantiation edges plus locally constructed receiver resolution for
    55 |   cross-file Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Java method calls
    56 | - Exact source spans, confidence, and unresolved-reference diagnostics
    57 | - Scalable React Flow visualization with on-demand neighborhood expansion
    58 | - Read-only Monaco source viewer and evidence inspector
    59 | - Claude-powered repository Q&A with bounded retrieval tools and validated citations
    60 | - revision-aware SQLite code indexing with persisted chunks, symbols, edges, file
    61 |   hashes, FTS5/BM25 search, and automatic refresh when repository contents change
    62 | - local subword-vector retrieval, reciprocal-rank fusion, graph expansion, index
    63 |   status/rebuild controls, and restart-safe issue/onboarding state
    64 | - pre/post/error function hooks, correlated model/tool/retrieval traces, rotating JSONL
    65 |   diagnostics, and a 30-tool MCP connector over stdio or Streamable HTTP
    66 | - readable GitHub-flavored Markdown rendering …<1000 chars truncated>

1 | # External repository benchmarks
     2 | 
     3 | This suite validates the analyzer against shallow clones of established Python
     4 | repositories. Clones live outside the application workspace by default at
     5 | `C:\tmp\waypoint-benchmarks`.
     6 | 
     7 | The benchmark verifies:
     8 | 
     9 | - Parse success and performance
    10 | - Unique, stable node and edge identities
    11 | - Valid graph endpoints
    12 | - Valid source spans
    13 | - Evidence-status invariants
    14 | - Correct package names for flat and `src/` layouts
    15 | - Known architectural modules, classes, methods, and functions
    16 | - First-party import resolution
    17 | 
    18 | Run:
    19 | 
    20 | ```powershell
    21 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_repositories.py `
    22 |   --fixtures-root C:\tmp\waypoint-benchmarks `
    23 |   --output benchmarks\results
    24 | ```
    25 | 
    26 | Use `--repository flask` to run one fixture. Results are written as JSON and
    27 | Markdown so changes in analyzer quality can be reviewed rather than inferred
    28 | from node counts alone.
    29 | 
    30 | ## Retrieval benchmark
    31 | 
    32 | The local retrieval benchmark measures file Hit@5, Hit@10, mean reciprocal rank,
    33 | nDCG@10, indexing/restoration time, cold/warm query latency, latency percentiles, and
    34 | process peak memory against known evidence files:
    35 | 
    36 | ```powershell
    37 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_retrieval.py `
    38 |   --repository . `
    39 |   --output benchmarks\results\retrieval-latest.json
    40 | ```
    41 | 
    42 | Add repository-specific cases by supplying another JSON file with `--cases`.
    43 | 
    44 | V3 also contains a 50-question, three-repository development benchmark with explicit
    45 | development/held-out labels, required path groups, forbidden distractors, repository and
    46 | language slices, and an adjudication gate. Pending seed labels are rejected unless the
    47 | caller explicitly opts into a non-release diagnostic:
    48 | 
    49 | ```powershell
    50 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_retrieval_v3.py `
    51 |   --repository waypoint=. `
    52 |   --repository flask=.waypoint-clones/pallets--flask--214023150b `
    53 |   --repository praw=.waypoint-clones/haxtheweb--praw--69db9269ab `
    54 |   --allow-unadjudicated `
    55 |   --output benchmarks\results\retrieval-v3.json
    56 | ```
    57 | 
    58 | See `BENCHMARKS_AND_TESTS_V3.md` for formulas, limitations, and the preserved V2-to-V3
    59 | comparison.
    60 | 
    61 | ## V4 independent-agent benchmark
    62 | 
    63 | V4 uses a separate 50-case, four-repository corpus. Each fixed endpoint independently
    64 | chooses production repository tools; candidate results, explicit source reads, and final
    65 | citations are scored separately. The benchmark also records schema corrections, retries,
    66 | tokens, latency, and trace-correlated hook/log quality.
    67 | 
    68 | ```powershell
    69 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_agentic_retrieval_v4.py `
    70 |   --repository waypoint=. `
    71 |   --repository flask=.waypoint-clones\pallets--flask--214023150b `
    72 |   --repository praw=.waypoint-clones\haxtheweb--praw--69db9269ab `
    73 |   --repository open-notebook=.waypoint-clones\lfnovo--open-notebook--5d0a28a4b0 `
    74 |   --endpoint openrouter:poolside/laguna-m.1:free `
    75 |   --endpoint openrouter:poolside/laguna-xs-2.1:free `
    76 |   --max-cases 50 `
    77 |   --allow-unadjudicated `
    78 |   --confirm-live-provider-usage `
    79 |   --output benchmarks\results\agentic-v4-poolside-campaign.json
    80 | ```
    81 | 
    82 | The current execution status and non-transient OpenRouter daily-quota blocker are

def clone(self, repository_url: str) -> Path:
        repository = parse_github_repository(repository_url)
        clone_root = self._validated_clone_root()
        git = shutil.which("git")
        if git is None:
            raise GitUnavailableError(
                "Git is not installed or is not available on the server PATH"
            )
        destination = clone_root / (
            f"{repository.owner}--{repository.name}--{uuid.uuid4().hex[:10]}"
        )
        destination.resolve().relative_to(clone_root)
        log_event(
            logger,
            logging.INFO,
            "repository.clone_requested",
            "Validated GitHub repository clone requested",
            owner=repository.owner,
            repository=repository.name,
            clone_url=repository.clone_url,
            destination=destination,
            shallow=True,
        )
        command = [
            git,
            "-c",
            "credential.helper=",
            "clone",
            "--depth",
            "1",

def run(base_url: str, repository_url: str, repository_path: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    with httpx.Client(base_url=base_url.rstrip("/"), timeout=300) as client:
        if repository_path:
            analysis_response = _request(
                client,
                "POST",
                "/api/v1/analysis",
                json={"repository_path": repository_path},
            )
        else:
            analysis_response = _request(
                client,
                "POST",
                "/api/v1/analysis/github",
                json={"repository_url": repository_url},
            )
        analysis = analysis_response.json()
        analysis_id = analysis["analysis_id"]
        assert analysis["stats"]["files_parsed"] >= 60, analysis["stats"]
        assert analysis["stats"]["parse_failures"] <= 3, analysis["stats"]
        source_paths = {
            node["span"]["path"]
            for node in analysis["nodes"]
            if node.get("span") and node["kind"] == "module"
        }
        expected = {"src/flask/__init__.py", "src/flask/app.py", "src/flask/cli.py"}
        assert expected.issubset(source_paths), sorted(expected - source_paths)

        summary = _request(
            client, "GET", f"/api/v1/analyses/{analysis_id}/summary"
        ).json()
        index = _request(
            client, "GET", f"/api/v1/analyses/{analysis_id}/index"
        ).json()
        source = _request(
            client,
            "GET",
            f"/api/v1/analyses/{analysis_id}/source",
            params={"path": "src/flask/app.py"},
        ).json()

def parse_file(self, path: Path) -> PolyglotModule | None:
        """Parses one non-Python source file with tree-sitter, enforces the byte-size limit, and creates its MODULE GraphNode.

        Input: an absolute file `path` beneath `self.root`. Returns `None`
        (after appending a diagnostic instead of raising) if the file exceeds
        `self.max_file_bytes`, isn't valid UTF-8, or fails to parse; a
        `parse_recovered` warning diagnostic is also recorded (without
        returning `None`) if tree-sitter's error-recovery kicked in, since the
        partial tree is still usable. Called once per discovered non-Python
        file by `RepositoryAnalyzer.analyze`, mirroring `_parse_file` in
        analyzer.py; returning `None` on failure lets one bad file be skipped
        without aborting the whole scan.
        """
        relative = path.relative_to(self.root).as_posix()
        size = path.stat().st_size
        language = _language_name(path)
        log_event(
            logger,
            logging.DEBUG,
            "parser.file_started",
            "Parsing Tree-sitter source file",
            path=relative,
            language=language,
            size_bytes=size,
        )
        if size > self.max_file_bytes:
            self.graph.diagnostics.append(
                AnalysisDiagnostic(
                    severity="warning",
                    code="file_too_large",
                    message=f"File is {size} bytes; limit is {self.max_file_bytes}",
                    path=relative,
                )
            )
            return None

def run(base_url: str, repository_url: str, repository_path: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    with httpx.Client(base_url=base_url.rstrip("/"), timeout=300) as client:
        if repository_path:
            analysis_response = _request(
                client,
                "POST",
                "/api/v1/analysis",
                json={"repository_path": repository_path},
            )
        else:
            analysis_response = _request(
                client,
                "POST",
                "/api/v1/analysis/github",
                json={"repository_url": repository_url},
            )
        analysis = analysis_response.json()
        analysis_id = analysis["analysis_id"]
        assert analysis["stats"]["files_parsed"] >= 60, analysis["stats"]
        assert analysis["stats"]["parse_failures"] <= 3, analysis["stats"]
        source_paths = {
            node["span"]["path"]
            for node in analysis["nodes"]
            if node.get("span") and node["kind"] == "module"
        }
        expected = {"src/flask/__init__.py", "src/flask/app.py", "src/flask/cli.py"}
        assert expected.issubset(source_paths), sorted(expected - source_paths)

        summary = _request(
            client, "GET", f"/api/v1/analyses/{analysis_id}/summary"
        ).json()
        index = _request(
            client, "GET", f"/api/v1/analyses/{analysis_id}/index"
        ).json()
        source = _request(
            client,
            "GET",
            f"/api/v1/analyses/{analysis_id}/source",
            params={"path": "src/flask/app.py"},
        ).json()

def _analyze(root: Path, repository_name: str | None = None) -> AnalysisReport:
    """Runs static analysis on a repository, stores the result, and returns its overview.

    Input: a resolved filesystem path to a repository root (already validated or
    freshly cloned) and an optional display name override. Runs
    RepositoryAnalyzer().analyze, persists the report as a new AnalysisSession via
    analysis_sessions.create, warms the retrieval index via repository_indexes.get,
    then returns GraphQueryService(...).overview(). Executed inside a threadpool by
    analyze_repository and analyze_github_repository, since analysis is CPU/IO
    heavy; this is the core pipeline that turns a submitted path or GitHub URL into
    a usable analysis_id for every other endpoint in this file.
    """
    report = RepositoryAnalyzer().analyze(root)
    if repository_name:
        report = report.model_copy(update={"repository_name": repository_name})
    stored = analysis_sessions.create(root, report)
    session = analysis_sessions.get(stored.analysis_id or "")
    repository_indexes.get(session)
    return GraphQueryService(session.report).overview()

## GitHub URL → Analysis: End-to-End Flow

Waypoint turns a public GitHub URL into a stored analysis through five bounded, security-conscious stages. The HTTP entry point is `POST /api/v1/analysis/github`, handled by `analyze_github_repository`, which delegates to a cloner and then an analyzer, each run in a threadpool.

### 1. URL validation

1 | # Waypoint — Adaptive Codebase Onboarding
     2 | 
     3 | Waypoint turns Python, JavaScript, TypeScript/TSX, Java, HTML, and CSS repositories into an
     4 | evidence-aware code graph and a role-specific onboarding workspace. It uses
     5 | static analysis only: analyzed repository code is never imported or executed.
     6 | 
     7 | ## Architecture
     8 | 
     9 | ```mermaid
    10 | flowchart TD
    11 |     UI[React + TypeScript UI] -->|HTTP /api/v1| API[FastAPI application]
    12 |     API --> IMPORT[Local path or secured GitHub clone]
    13 |     IMPORT --> ANALYZER[Python AST + Tree-sitter analyzers]
    14 |     ANALYZER --> GRAPH[Typed code graph]
    15 |     ANALYZER --> INDEX[Revision-aware SQLite index]
    16 |     INDEX --> SEARCH[FTS5/BM25 + local vectors]
    17 |     GRAPH --> SEARCH
    18 |     API --> MEMORY[SQLite conversations and sessions]
    19 |     API --> AGENT[Repository agent runner]
    20 |     AGENT --> INVESTIGATE[Investigation model]
    21 |     INVESTIGATE --> TOOLS[Bounded repository tools]
    22 |     TOOLS --> SEARCH
    23 |     TOOLS --> GRAPH
    24 |     AGENT --> SYNTHESIZE[Synthesis model]
    25 |     SYNTHESIZE --> VALIDATE[Pydantic tool + answer + citation validation]
    26 |     VALIDATE --> UI
    27 |     UI --> COMPARE[Independent two-agent comparison]
    28 |     COMPARE --> TOOLS
    29 |     MCP[MCP server: 30 tools] --> GRAPH
    30 |     MCP --> SEARCH
    31 |     HOOKS[Pre / post / error hooks and JSONL traces] -.observe.-> API
    32 |     HOOKS -.observe.-> AGENT
    33 |     HOOKS -.observe.-> TOOLS
    34 | ```
    35 | 
    36 | FastAPI and Pydantic provide typed HTTP boundaries and generated OpenAPI; React,
    37 | TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, React Flow, and Monaco provide the interactive evidence
    38 | workspace. SQLite keeps the project locally deployable while persisting graph sessions,
    39 | chunks, lexical/vector indexes, issues, and conversation memory. The model layer supports
    40 | OpenRouter, the Anthropic API, and the Claude Agent SDK. In dual mode a low-cost model can
    41 | investigate through tools while a stronger model synthesizes a validated answer.
    42 | 
    43 | The detailed verification package, including coverage, Flask HTTP E2E, live multi-step
    44 | agent evidence, and same-question two-model comparison, is in
    45 | [`verification/README.md`](verification/README.md). Significant AI-assisted engineering
    46 | interactions are recorded in [`prompts.md`](prompts.md).
    47 | 
    48 | ## What is included
    49 | 
    50 | - Python AST extraction for modules, classes, functions, methods, imports, and calls

1 | # External repository benchmarks
     2 | 
     3 | This suite validates the analyzer against shallow clones of established Python
     4 | repositories. Clones live outside the application workspace by default at
     5 | `C:\tmp\waypoint-benchmarks`.
     6 | 
     7 | The benchmark verifies:
     8 | 
     9 | - Parse success and performance
    10 | - Unique, stable node and edge identities
    11 | - Valid graph endpoints
    12 | - Valid source spans
    13 | - Evidence-status invariants
    14 | - Correct package names for flat and `src/` layouts
    15 | - Known architectural modules, classes, methods, and functions
    16 | - First-party import resolution
    17 | 
    18 | Run:
    19 | 
    20 | ```powershell
    21 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_repositories.py `
    22 |   --fixtures-root C:\tmp\waypoint-benchmarks `
    23 |   --output benchmarks\results
    24 | ```
    25 | 
    26 | Use `--repository flask` to run one fixture. Results are written as JSON and
    27 | Markdown so changes in analyzer quality can be reviewed rather than inferred
    28 | from node counts alone.
    29 | 
    30 | ## Retrieval benchmark
    31 | 
    32 | The local retrieval benchmark measures file Hit@5, Hit@10, mean reciprocal rank,
    33 | nDCG@10, indexing/restoration time, cold/warm query latency, latency percentiles, and
    34 | process peak memory against known evidence files:
    35 | 
    36 | ```powershell
    37 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_retrieval.py `
    38 |   --repository . `
    39 |   --output benchmarks\results\retrieval-latest.json
    40 | ```
    41 | 
    42 | Add repository-specific cases by supplying another JSON file with `--cases`.
    43 | 
    44 | V3 also contains a 50-question, three-repository development benchmark with explicit
    45 | development/held-out labels, required path groups, forbidden distractors, repository and
    46 | language slices, and an adjudication gate. Pending seed labels are rejected unless the
    47 | caller explicitly opts into a non-release diagnostic:
    48 | 
    49 | ```powershell
    50 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_retrieval_v3.py `
    51 |   --repository waypoint=. `
    52 |   --repository flask=.waypoint-clones/pallets--flask--214023150b `
    53 |   --repository praw=.waypoint-clones/haxtheweb--praw--69db9269ab `
    54 |   --allow-unadjudicated `
    55 |   --output benchmarks\results\retrieval-v3.json
    56 | ```
    57 | 
    58 | See `BENCHMARKS_AND_TESTS_V3.md` for formulas, limitations, and the preserved V2-to-V3
    59 | comparison.
    60 | 
    61 | ## V4 independent-agent benchmark
    62 | 
    63 | V4 uses a separate 50-case, four-repository corpus. Each fixed endpoint independently
    64 | chooses production repository tools; candidate results, explicit source reads, and final
    65 | citations are scored separately. The benchmark also records schema corrections, retries,
    66 | tokens, latency, and trace-correlated hook/log quality.
    67 | 
    68 | ```powershell
    69 | .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe benchmarks\run_agentic_retrieval_v4.py `
    70 |   --repository waypoint=. `
    71 |   --repository flask=.waypoint-clones\pallets--flask--214023150b `
    72 |   --repository praw=.waypoint-clones\haxtheweb--praw--69db9269ab `
    73 |   --repository open-notebook=.waypoint-clones\lfnovo--open-notebook--5d0a28a4b0 `
    74 |   --endpoint openrouter:poolside/laguna-m.1:free `
    75 |   --endpoint openrouter:poolside/laguna-xs-2.1:free `
    76 |   --max-cases 50 `
    77 |   --allow-unadjudicated `
    78 |   --confirm-live-provider-usage `
    79 |   --output benchmarks\results\agentic-v4-poolside-campaign.json
    80 | ```
    81 | 
    82 | The current execution status and non-transient OpenRouter daily-quota blocker are
    83 | documented in `BENCHMARKS_AND_TESTS_V4.md`.

def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Build Waypoint's operational service scorecard")
    parser.add_argument("--threshold", type=float, default=0.70)
    parser.add_argument("--model-result", type=Path, default=Path("verification/results/model-quality-claude-code-openrouter.json"))
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=Path("verification/results/operational-scorecard.json"))
    arguments = parser.parse_args()
    paths = {
        "parsing": Path("benchmarks/results/parsing-accuracy.json"),
        "retrieval": Path("benchmarks/results/retrieval-v2.json"),
        "performance": Path("verification/results/service-performance.json"),
        "model": arguments.model_result,
        "playwright": Path("frontend/test-results/results.json"),
        "frontend_coverage": Path("frontend/coverage/coverage-summary.json"),
        "frontend_performance": Path("verification/results/frontend-performance.json"),
    }
    result = build(paths, arguments.threshold)
    arguments.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    arguments.output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    markdown = _markdown(result)
    arguments.output.with_suffix(".md").write_text(markdown + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(markdown)

def _frontend(playwright: dict[str, Any], coverage: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    suites = playwright.get("suites", [])
    tests: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    def visit(items: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
        for item in items:
            tests.extend(item.get("specs", []))
            visit(item.get("suites", []))

    visit(suites)
    executed = [spec for spec in tests if spec.get("tests", [{}])[0].get("status") != "skipped"]
    passed = sum(
        all(test.get("status") == "expected" for test in spec.get("tests", []))
        for spec in executed
    )
    e2e_success = passed / max(1, len(executed))
    line_percent = float(coverage.get("total", {}).get("lines", {}).get("pct", 0)) / 100
    return {
        "score": round((e2e_success + line_percent) / 2, 4),
        "e2e_success_rate": round(e2e_success, 4),
        "frontend_line_coverage": round(line_percent, 4),
        "executed_tests": len(executed),
        "skipped_tests": len(tests) - len(executed),
    }

def build(paths: dict[str, Path], threshold: float) -> dict[str, Any]:
    parsing = _load(paths["parsing"])
    retrieval = _load(paths["retrieval"])
    performance = _load(paths["performance"])
    model = _load(paths["model"])
    playwright = _load(paths["playwright"])
    frontend_coverage = _load(paths["frontend_coverage"])
    frontend_performance = _load(paths["frontend_performance"])
    categories: dict[str, Any] = {}
    missing = []

    if parsing:
        values = [
            parsing["parse_success_rate"],
            parsing["node_metrics"]["f1"],
            parsing["edge_metrics"]["f1"],
        ]
        categories["parsing_accuracy"] = {
            "score": round(statistics.mean(values), 4),
            "parse_success_rate": values[0],
            "node_f1": values[1],
            "edge_f1": values[2],
        }
    else:
        missing.append("parsing_accuracy")

    if retrieval:
        strict_score = retrieval.get("strict_quality_score")
        values = [
            retrieval["hit_rate_at_5"],
            retrieval["hit_rate_at_10"],
            retrieval["mean_reciprocal_rank"],
            retrieval["ndcg_at_10"],
        ]
        categories["retrieval_quality"] = {
            "score": round(strict_score if strict_score is not None else statistics.mean(values), 4),
            "hit_rate_at_5": values[0],
            "hit_rate_at_10": values[1],
            "mrr": values[2],

## Is Waypoint agentic RAG over graph nodes?

Waypoint is agentic hybrid RAG over several evidence channels, not graph nodes alone.
The model can choose repository-search, bounded source-reading, symbol, graph, semantic,
test, configuration, and diagnostic tools over multiple rounds. Retrieved results are
added to its conversation before it synthesizes an answer.

The evidence channels are:

1. Parser-derived graph nodes and typed edges.
2. Symbol-aware source chunks.
3. SQLite FTS5/BM25 lexical retrieval.
4. Deterministic local subword-vector retrieval.
5. Exact path, qualified-name, symbol-kind, and test-aware ranking signals.
6. Bounded graph-neighbor expansion around strong retrieved symbols.

## What are the graph nodes?

`backend/app/graph/models.py:9-15` defines five node kinds:

| Node | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `repository` | The analyzed repository as the graph root. |
| `module` | An analyzed source file/module. |
| `class` | A parser-discovered class or interface-like type. |
| `function` | A module-level or nested function. |
| `method` | A callable owned by a class. |

Nodes carry a stable ID, kind, short name, qualified name, module, source span,
signature, and metadata. They are static source-code entities, not runtime objects.
A runtime-like construction such as `UserService()` is represented as an
`instantiates` edge to the class node rather than a separate object-instance node.

The typed edges are:

- `contains`: repository/module/class lexical ownership;
- `imports`: one internal module imports another;
- `may_call`: a st

# Graph nodes and vector validity

## Is Waypoint agentic RAG over graph nodes?

Waypoint is agentic hybrid RAG over several evidence channels, not graph nodes alone.
The model can choose repository-search, bounded source-reading, symbol, graph, semantic,
test, configuration, and diagnostic tools over multiple rounds. Retrieved results are
added to its conversation before it synthesizes an answer.

The evidence channels are:

1. Parser-derived graph nodes and typed edges.
2. Symbol-aware source chunks.
3. SQLite FTS5/BM25 lexical retrieval.
4. Deterministic local subword-vector retrieval.
5. Exact path, qualified-name, symbol-kind, and test-aware ranking signals.
6. Bounded graph-neighbor expansion around strong retrieved symbols.

## What are the graph nodes?

`backend/app/graph/models.py:9-15` defines five node kinds:

| Node | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `repository` | The analyzed repository as the graph root. |
| `module` | An analyzed source file/module. |
| `class` | A parser-discovered class or interface-like type. |
| `function` | A module-level or nested function. |
| `method` | A callable owned by a class. |

Nodes carry a stable ID, kind, short name, qualified name, module, source span,
signature, and metadata. They are static source-code entities, not runtime objects.
A runtime-like construction such as `UserService()` is represented as an
`instantiates` edge to the class node rather than a separate object-instance node.

The typed edges are:

- `contains`: repository/module/class lexical ownership;
- `imports`: one internal module imports another;
- `may_call`: a st

## 1. Files → file cards

When the graph view is in the **files** presentation mode, `GraphCanvas` (frontend/src/components/GraphView.tsx) builds one card per source file through two steps:

1. `fileGroups()` (GraphView.tsx:142-213) groups every graph node by its source path (`nodePath()`, GraphView.tsx:82-85, reads `node.span.path`, or a synthetic `__waypoint__/external-packages` path for external imports). For each path it produces a `FileGroup` containing:
   - `primary`: the file's `module` node (or first member if none), used for the card header/language label.
   - `members`: the symbols in that file that currently pass the visible-node-kind filter and the search text filter.
   - `uses`: symbols from *other* files that this file references (derived by walking every non-`contains` edge whose source and target live in different files and collecting the target nodes), also kind/search filtered.
   - `externalPackages`: populated only for the synthetic external-packages group (built by `externalPackageGraph()`, GraphView.tsx:87-140, from `unresolvedReferences` whose `reference_kind === "import"` and `metadata.external === true`).

2. `layoutFileGraph()` (GraphView.tsx:215-383) turns each `FileGroup` into a React Flow `Node`: it sizes the card from `FILE_NODE_SIZES[cardSize]` (compact/comfortable/large, chosen by the user's `fileCardSize` setting), lays cards out left-to-right with `dagre`, and renders the card body as a header (language + filename + path), a scrollable member list (each member is a clickable `<button>` that calls `onSelect({ type: "node", value: member })`), an optional "Uses across files" section (also clickable), and a footer summarizing visible-symbol/external-use counts.

`GraphCanvas` computes this via `useMemo` keyed on `props.presentation === "files"`, so switching workspace modes rebuilds the cards from the same underlying `nodes`/`edges`/`unresolvedReferences` props supplied by `App.tsx`.

## 2. How visible graph edges are selected

Edge visibility is filtered in two layers before layout:

- **Kind filter**: a `Set<EdgeKind>` (`visibleEdgeKinds`, driven by UI toggles for `contains`/`imports`/`may_call`/`instantiates`) is checked first; edges of a hidden kind are skipped everywhere (`fileGroups`, `layoutFileGraph`).
- **Endpoint filter**: in **file mode** (`layoutFileGraph`, GraphView.tsx:231-245), an edge is kept only if both its source and target nodes resolve to a file path (`pathByNode`), the two files differ (self-file edges are dropped since they'd be a same-card loop), and both files are in the currently included/visible group set. result.answer:
## 1. Files → file cards

When the graph view is in the **files** presentation mode, `GraphCanvas` (frontend/src/components/GraphView.tsx) builds one card per source file through two steps:

1. `fileGroups()` (GraphView.tsx:142-213) groups every graph node by its source path (`nodePath()`, GraphView.tsx:82-85, reads `node.span.path`, or a synthetic `__waypoint__/external-packages` path for external imports). For each path it produces a `FileGroup` containing:
   - `primary`: the file's `module` node (or first member if none), used for the card header/language label.
   - `members`: the symbols in that file that currently pass the visible-node-kind filter and the search text filter.
   - `uses`: symbols from *other* files that this file references (derived by walking every non-`contains` edge whose source and target live in different files and collecting the target nodes), also kind/search filtered.
   - `externalPackages`: populated only for the synthetic external-packages group (built by `externalPackageGraph()`, GraphView.tsx:87-140, from `unresolvedReferences` whose `reference_kind === "import"` and `metadata.external === true`).
   Groups with zero visible members and no matching external packages are dropped, and remaining groups are sorted by path.
2. `layoutFileGraph()` (GraphView.tsx:215-383) turns each `FileGroup` into a React Flow `Node`: it sizes the card from `FILE_NODE_SIZES[cardSize]` (compact/comfortable/large, chosen by the user's `fileCardSize` setting), lays cards out left-to-right with `dagre`, and renders the card body as a header (language + filename + path), a scrollable member list (each member is a clickable `<button>` that calls `onSelect({ type: "node", value: member })`), an optional "Uses across files" section (also clickable), and a footer summarizing visible-symbol/external-use counts.

`GraphCanvas` computes this via `useMemo` keyed on `props.presentation === "files"`, so switching workspace modes rebuilds the cards from the same underlying `nodes`/`edges`/`unresolvedReferences` props supplied by `App.tsx`.

## 2. How visible graph edges are selected

Edge visibility is filtered in two layers before layout:

- **Kind filter**: a `Set<EdgeKind>` (`visibleEdgeKinds`, driven by UI toggles for `contains`/`imports`/`may_call`/`instantiates`) is checked first; edges of a hidden kind are skipped everywhere (`fileGroups`, `layoutFileGraph`).
- **Endpoint filter**: in **file mode** (`layoutFileGraph`, GraphView.tsx:231-245), an edge is kept only if both its source and target nodes resolve to a file path (`pathByNode`), the two files differ (self-file edges are dropped since they'd be a same-card loop), and both files are in the currently included/visible group set. Multiple underlying edges between the same file pair and kind are merged into a single visual edge keyed by `source␀target␀kind`, with the merged edge's line drawn thicker for more underlying edges and labeled with the count when >1.

    13 |     IMPORT --> ANALYZER[Python AST + Tree-sitter analyzers]
    14 |     ANALYZER --> GRAPH[Typed code graph]
    15 |     ANALYZER --> INDEX[Revision-aware SQLite index]
    16 |     INDEX --> SEARCH[FTS5/BM25 + local vectors]
    17 |     GRAPH --> SEARCH
    18 |     API --> MEMORY[SQLite conversations and sessions]
    19 |     API --> AGENT[Repository agent runner]
    20 |     AGENT --> INVESTIGATE[Investigation model]
    21 |     INVESTIGATE --> TOOLS[Bounded repository tools]
    22 |     TOOLS --> SEARCH
    23 |     TOOLS --> GRAPH
    24 |     AGENT --> SYNTHESIZE[Synthesis model]
    25 |     SYNTHESIZE --> VALIDATE[Pydantic tool + answer + citation validation]

    36 | FastAPI and Pydantic provide typed HTTP boundaries and generated OpenAPI; React,
    37 | TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, React Flow, and Monaco provide the interactive evidence
    38 | workspace. SQLite keeps the project locally deployable while persisting graph sessions,
    39 | chunks, lexical/vector indexes, issues, and conversation memory. The model layer supports
    40 | OpenRouter, the Anthropic API, and the Claude Agent SDK. In dual mode a low-cost model can
    41 | investigate through tools while a stronger model synthesizes a validated answer.
    42 | 
    43 | The detailed verification package, including coverage, Flask HTTP E2E, live multi-step
    44 | agent evidence, and same-question two-model comparison, is in
    45 | [`verification/README.md`](verification/README.md). Significant AI-assisted engineering
    46 | interactions are recorded in [`prompts.md`](prompts.md).

    52 | - ES module imports/re-exports, CommonJS `require`, Java packages/imports, lexical

    62 | - local subword-vector retrieval, reciprocal-rank fusion, graph expansion, index

    64 | - pre/post/error function hooks, correlated model/tool/retrieval traces, rotating JSONL
    65 |   diagnostics, and a 30-tool MCP connector over stdio or Streamable HTTP

def _edge_evidence(self, edge: GraphEdge) -> dict[str, Any] | None:

        the edge was inferred from; reads a narrow window (one line before to up to
        eight lines after) capped at 2,000 characters, since edges need only enough
        context to show the reference, not the whole containing function. Called by
        symbol_relationships to back each incoming/outgoing relationship with the
        actual line of code that produced it.

        return {
            "path": source["path"],

            "end_line": source["end_line"],

    """Enumerates the kinds of relationship a GraphEdge can represent.

    CONTAINS is lexical containment (module contains class contains method),
    IMPORTS is a module-level import, MAY_CALL is an inferred call edge, and
    INSTANTIATES is class construction. Built wherever a GraphEdge is created in
    analyzer.py/polyglot.py and read back by store.py's GraphQueryService to
    bucket edges by kind for the graph summary and neighborhood views.
    """

    CONTAINS = "contains"
    IMPORTS = "imports"
    MAY_CALL = "may_call"
    INSTANTIATES = "instantiates"

def _edge_evidence(self, edge: GraphEdge) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        """Reads a small source excerpt around the line where a graph edge (call/import/etc.) was detected.

        Input: `edge` is a GraphEdge whose `evidence.span` marks the source location
        the edge was inferred from; reads a narrow window (one line before to up to
        eight lines after) capped at 2,000 characters, since edges need only enough
        context to show the reference, not the whole containing function. Called by
        symbol_relationships to back each incoming/outgoing relationship with the
        actual line of code that produced it.
        """
        span = edge.evidence.span
        try:
            source = self.index.read(
                span.path,
                max(1, span.start_line - 1),
                min(span.end_line + 1, span.start_line + 8),
            )
        except ValueError:
            return None
        return {
            "path": source["path"],
            "start_line": source["start_line"],
            "end_line": source["end_line"],
            "edge_id": edge.id,
            "relationship": edge.kind.value,
            "excerpt": source["content"][:2_000],
